segments.script: First, meaning. I read “I could easily forgive his pride, if he had not mortified mine” slowly and put it in my own words: Elizabeth says she could forgive Darcy's pride if he had not hurt her own. Next, craft. I notice the balanced sentence, his pride against hers, which turns the joke on herself. The strongest word is “mortified”: it means wounded, humiliated, which shows her dislike starts with a personal insult. Then, effect. What does Elizabeth's joke show about why she dislikes Darcy? My answer: Elizabeth's joke that she could forgive Darcy's pride if he had not mortified hers shows that she dislikes Darcy from wounded pride, not fairness; it names both title faults in one speaker.
